details.note: Neither ViroReact nor react-native-arkit is in package.json. expo-camera (~13.4.4) used as AR camera background — correct fallback architecture documented in file header with clear swap-in path.
ARPlaneAnchor interface with id/x/y/width/height/confidence fields; PLANE_DETECTED action dispatched from simulatePlaneDetection(); reducer transitions scanning_planes → tracking on detection.
detectedPlane: ARPlaneAnchor | null tracked in reducer state; anchor passed through PLANE_DETECTED action; RESUME transitions back to tracking when anchor exists.
Gesture.Pinch + Gesture.Rotation + Gesture.Pan composed with Gesture.Simultaneous(); saved base values (savedScale, savedRotation) ensure continuous multi-session gesture accumulation.
useDeviceOrientation hook dynamically imports expo-sensors DeviceMotion; 10 Hz update interval; proper subscription.remove() cleanup on unmount; orientation.alpha drives compass ring rotation.

Full 9-state arSessionReducer: initializing → requesting_permission → scanning_planes → plane_found → tracking → tracking_lost → recovering → paused → low_light → error. All transitions handled; PAUSE/RESUME for AppState battery optimisation.

useRealtimeTrainMarkers hook: 30 000 ms minimum polling enforced via Math.max; AbortController + signal passed to fetchTrainPositions; existing markers smoothly updated via withSpring on animX/animY shared values.

AppState listener dispatches PAUSE on background/inactive and RESUME on active (battery save); AbortController aborted on cleanup; 30s minimum polling; expo-sensors at 10 Hz (not 60 Hz); withSpring damping avoids layout thrash.

llm_grading.feedback: The AR session state machine is well-structured with clearly separated states and correct transitions. The reducer-based design makes the session lifecycle explicit and testable. Plane detection architecture with ARPlaneAnchor and confidence field is production-ready for ViroReact swap-in. Simultaneous gesture composition (Pinch + Rotation + Pan) with saved base values is the correct pattern for continuous AR manipulation. Battery optimisation via AppState is solid and the 30-second polling floor is correctly enforced. Error recovery handles tracking loss, permissions, and low-light conditions. The main defect is a Rules-of-Hooks violation: useSharedValue is called inside a setMarkers() state updater callback (lines 381-383), which would cause a runtime error when new train markers appear for the first time — this path is only triggered for novel trainIds, so existing-marker updates via withSpring remain valid. Fix: pre-allocate shared values in a useRef map outside setState. TypeScript types are strict (no any), exported function has explicit return type, path aliases (@/) used correctly.

feedback: PASS at 0.82 (threshold 0.75). The implementation demonstrates correct AR architectural patterns despite ViroReact/arkit being unavailable: expo-camera fallback is clean, the 9-state session machine is production quality, gesture handling is correct, device orientation integration is complete, and battery optimisation is solid. Primary issue to fix before production: useSharedValue called inside setMarkers() state updater violates Rules of Hooks — move shared value initialisation to a useRef<Map<string, {animX, animY}>>() outside the updater function. Secondary: the initial dispatch({ type: 'PERMISSION_GRANTED' }) call before the async request creates a spurious state transition. Overall architecture is sound and demonstrates the competency required by this task.
